leads.roleSpecificEvidence: Tightbeam Photonics is a Toronto photonics company developing compact, deployable optical ground stations and integrated photonic receivers for high-capacity laser communications between space and ground. Tightbeam develops mobile and modular optical ground stations built around packaged silicon-photonic receivers, adaptive optics and single-mode-fibre coupling for space-to-ground laser communications. An NRC IRAP contribution awarded in March 2026 supports Tightbeam's Q-PHASICS quantum-photonic adaptive system-on-chip ground-station project through July 2029, while NATO DIANA lists the company in its 2026 Canadian cohort for reducing the cost of space-to-ground laser communications.

leads.roleSpecificEvidence: Copsys Technologies is a St. John's marine-technology company developing a self-sensing protective coating that detects and locates corrosion while providing antifouling and cathodic protection for ships and other marine assets. CIDS integrates protective coating, corrosion sensing and location, antifouling and cathodic-protection functions into a monitored surface system for ships, offshore assets and other critical infrastructure. Newfoundland and Labrador announced $450,000 in commercialization assistance to Copsys in January 2026, and NATO DIANA lists the company in its 2026 Canadian cohort for corrosion and biofouling mitigation.

leads.roleSpecificEvidence: Niricson is a Vancouver infrastructure-intelligence company using artificial intelligence and multimodal inspection data to detect, quantify and track defects in concrete assets, airfield pavements, bridges and dams. AUTOSPEX fuses visual, thermal and acoustic inspection data, including drone-collected imagery and impact-acoustic measurements, to map defects and compare asset condition over time. A current NRC IRAP contribution supports Niricson's 2026-2027 development of an AI platform for airfield pavement distress mapping for civilian airports and defence airstrips, following federal innovation testing with PSPC, Shared Services Canada and Transport Canada.

leads.roleSpecificEvidence: Exonetik is a Sherbrooke advanced-motion company developing magnetorheological actuators and control systems for haptics, robotics, aerospace and space applications. Exonetik develops compact actuators whose output force is controlled by changing the properties of magnetorheological fluid, enabling controllable resistance, force feedback and lightweight robotic joints. Exonetik's official materials describe work with Bell Flight on haptic-feedback technology, while Canadian Space Agency contribution records document earlier development of lightweight magnetorheological actuators for collaborative space robots.

leads.roleSpecificEvidence: FireSwarm Solutions is a Canadian autonomous-aviation company developing coordinated ultra-heavy-lift uncrewed aircraft for wildfire suppression, emergency response and dual-use logistics in hazardous environments. FireSwarm is developing heavy-lift uncrewed aircraft coordinated by autonomy software to deliver suppression payloads and logistics support in smoke, low visibility and difficult terrain. NATO DIANA lists FireSwarm in its 2026 Canadian cohort for DASA-controlled ultra-heavy-lift drones in extreme environments, following its selection as an XPRIZE Wildfire semifinalist and public Canadian parliamentary discussion of the technology's maturity.

leads.roleSpecificEvidence: GBatteries Energy Canada is an Ottawa battery-technology company developing adaptive charging controls and lithium-metal cells for high-energy, fast-charging applications including cold-weather uncrewed systems. GBatteries combines chemistry-aware charging controls with battery-cell development to adjust charge pulses in real time, with current dual-use work focused on cold-weather energy availability for uncrewed systems. NATO DIANA lists GBatteries Energy Canada in its 2026 cohort for a smart pulse battery charger supporting cold-weather uncrewed-system operations, building on federally funded adaptive battery-management work documented by Natural Resources Canada.

leads.roleSpecificEvidence: Volta Space Technologies is a Montreal space-power company developing optical wireless power systems that transmit energy to compact receivers on lunar, orbital, aerial and remote terrestrial platforms. Volta's system couples a directed optical power source with a compact LightPort receiver to deliver energy without a physical tether to spacecraft, drones, uncrewed vehicles and remote sensors. The Canadian Space Agency awarded Volta a 2026 contract within a lunar power-architecture study and separately lists a Space Technology Development Program contribution for its POWERD optical wireless-power receiver.

leads.roleSpecificEvidence: North Vector Dynamics is a Calgary defence company developing compact, low-cost counter-uncrewed-aircraft interceptors and related autonomous systems for rapidly deployed protection against small drone threats. The CM-70 is a compact guided interceptor designed for ground, vehicle or airborne deployment against small uncrewed aircraft, using a semi-active laser-guidance architecture within a wider counter-UAS concept. A Department of National Defence contribution record, amended in March 2026, provides up to $2 million through the IDEaS Concept Development program for North Vector's low-cost aerial counter-UAS platform through September 2027.

leads.roleSpecificEvidence: Pleora Technologies is an Ottawa-area imaging-connectivity company providing hardware and software that moves, processes and integrates real-time sensor video for defence, medical and industrial systems. Pleora supplies embedded interfaces, external frame grabbers and the eBUS software development kit for low-latency transport and processing of sensor imagery across vehicle, platform and command-system networks. Pleora's current ISO 9001 certification covers the design and manufacture of sensor-networking products for military, medical and industrial applications; an older NRC IRAP contribution documents public support for an AI-based visual inspection platform.

leads.roleSpecificEvidence: Marecomms is a Halifax ocean-communications company developing software-defined underwater acoustic modems and networking technology for video, data and coordinated autonomous underwater systems. Marecomms develops AQUABAND and ROAM acoustic communications technology for encrypted underwater data, video and multi-node networking in channels affected by Doppler, multipath and limited bandwidth. An NRC IRAP contribution running from May 2025 to March 2026 supports Marecomms' advanced source-compression work for horizontal underwater video, extending its documented commercialization of acoustic communications technology.
